item.title: Optimal Rates for Federated Variational Inequalities under different relaxations of bounded variance assumption
item.description: arXiv:2610.12641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how interpolation affects local steps and parallel sampling in monotone variational inequalities (VIs), with $m$ workers, $K$ oracle calls per worker per round, and $N$ rounds. Under the strong growth condition (SGC), we determine the minimax rate for affine VIs, attained by local extragradient with worker averaging. For nonlinear monotone VIs and convex-concave saddle problems with Lipschitz operators satisfying SGC, we improve the stochastic terms of bounded-variance expected-gap guarantees from $(KN)^{-1/2}$ to $(KN)^{-1}$ with local steps and from $(mKN)^{-1/2}$ to $(mKN)^{-1}$ with minibatches. Under strong monotonicity, we improve the noise-dependent condition-number scaling of existing extragradient bounds from quadratic to linear. The resulting monotone-gap and strongly monotone accuracy bounds match lower bounds up to logarithmic factors in $m$. Under generalized smoothness and SGC, adaptive steps give polynomial dependence on the initial radius. For affine VIs with globally bounded oracle variance, we also attain the minimax rate: the deterministic rate over $KN$ sequential calls plus the statistical rate over all $mKN$ samples. For composite VIs with smooth convex sample interpolation and an exactly evaluated monotone Lipschitz component, accelerated mirror-prox sliding achieves an $N^{-2}$ gradient term, a $(KN)^{-1}$ monotone term, and a $(mKN)^{-1}$ sampling term, without assuming SGC.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Novoselov, Yuriy Dorn, Darina Dvinskikh, Alexander Gasnikov

item.title: Complexity of Multiblock Convex-Concave Saddle-Point Problems with General Smooth Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.12656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study multiblock convex--concave saddle-point problems of the form $\min_x\max_y\{f(x)+H(x,y)-g(y)\}$, with separately charged partial-gradient oracles for all three objective components. We impose joint smoothness and strong convexity bounds on the functions $f$ and $g$, together with blockwise Lipschitz conditions on the partial gradients of $H$, so that the resulting oracle complexities reflect the smoothness and dependency parameters specific to each oracle. Under strong convexity, we develop a randomized lifted extragradient method that achieves linear convergence while providing simultaneous complexity guarantees for all oracles. The partial-gradient complexities for $f$ and $g$ exhibit the expected square-root dependence on the corresponding block condition numbers, whereas the coupling-gradient complexities depend on the associated curvature-normalized smoothness parameters. Finite-dimensional bilinear subclasses provide lower-complexity benchmarks within a randomized blockwise linear-span model. When strong convexity of $f$ and $g$ is not assumed, a regularization argument yields expected restricted-gap guarantees with accuracy dependence $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ for the objective-gradient oracles and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for the coupling-gradient oracles, up to logarithmic factors. Experiments show observed oracle savings and runtime improvements in regimes of poor objective conditioning.
item.dc:creator: Nhat Trung Nguyen, Ivan Dorofeev, Irina Podlipnova, Yuriy Dorn, Alexander Gasnikov

item.title: On the 100% Rule of Linear Programming
item.description: arXiv:2610.12665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The so-called ``100% rule'' is a somewhat classical and yet somehow obscure rule that gives some local sensitivity-analysis information based on the very limited local sensitivity-analysis information that is often made available by linear-programming software, derived from an optimal basis that is hidden from the user. Introduced in a classic undergraduate textbook in 1977, half a century ago, it was only picked up on by researchers in a very limited way, and while it appears in some undergraduate textbooks, it tends not to appear in most modern graduate-level textbooks. Our contributions are to celebrate and revive interest in the 100% rule and to extend it in a meaningful way. We introduce a cone rule that certifies primal feasibility for more right-hand sides than the 100% rule does, using the same information, and that can be applied in linear time. We then study when this cone rule is tight, that is, when it captures the entire cone of right-hand sides for which the basis remains feasible. We characterize tightness in every dimension for right-hand sides interior to that cone, make the characterization explicit for m=2 and m=3, and settle the question for tridiagonal bases in every dimension: tightness is impossible once m>=4, and for m=3 we give an explicit criterion in the entries of the basis. We give further results for symmetric, integer and unimodular bases. Finally, when tightness fails, we measure the fraction of the feasibility cone captured by the rule using normalized solid angles. For the autoregressive family at m=3, we obtain a closed-form candidate for the infimum of this fraction over all right-hand sides, whose optimality is supported numerically. We also obtain a closed-form expression for the best case over most of the correlation range, subject to two numerically verified properties, and estimate the best-case value numerically more generally.
item.dc:creator: Marcia Fampa, Jon Lee

item.title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
item.description: arXiv:2610.12697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.
item.dc:creator: Zeru Zhu, Marco Gamarra, Ji Liu

item.title: SDDP has polynomial iteration complexity in the horizon
item.description: arXiv:2610.12713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) and its variants are run in practice with forward passes that sample the noise at random. Recent iteration-complexity results favour another choice: when the trial points are selected deterministically, for instance along the scenario with the largest gap, the number of iterations is polynomial in the horizon $T$, whereas every bound we know of for randomly sampled forward passes is exponential in $T$. We show that this is not intrinsic to random sampling, for a broad class of trajectory-following dynamic programming algorithms, which includes SDDP, stochastic dual dynamic integer programming and stochastic Lipschitz dynamic programming. With random sampling, and with Lipschitz constants, diameters and per-stage loss ranges bounded independently of the stage and of the horizon, the expected number of iterations whose policy is not $T\varepsilon$-optimal is $O(T\varepsilon^{-(d+1)})$, where $d$ is the state dimension: linear in $T$, as for deterministic selection rules. The proof needs no particular scenario to be sampled: the gap between the expected cost of the current policy and the current lower bound equals the expected sum of one-step Bellman residuals along the sampled path, and Lipschitz cuts that are tight at the visited states turn the positive residuals into permanent increases of a bounded potential. The results extend to noise without finite support, to backward passes on a sample average approximation, and to stationary and periodic infinite-horizon SDDP with geometric pass lengths.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Leclere

item.title: Childcare Waitlists
item.description: arXiv:2610.12732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parents seeking childcare often face long waitlists. At the same time, vacancies at childcare centers can remain unfilled for extended periods. We trace this paradox to two persistent features of childcare services. First, families consider multiple child care options due to enrollment uncertainties, resulting in phantom listings that remain on waitlists even after families have found care elsewhere or no longer need a slot. Second, filling a slot is time-consuming: centers learn whether a family is actively seeking enrollment only after making an offer and waiting for a response. As families pursue alternatives while they wait and their children age, these delays and feedback effects amplify the mismatch between demand and available capacity. We study two operational remedies. First, we examine regular verification that removes phantom listings before offers are made, improving the efficiency of enrollment and reducing vacancies. Second, we study mixed-age classrooms, in which some slots designated for older children can be flexibly used by younger children. This flexibility increases utilization, shortens waits, and reduces wasted offers. Its benefits extend beyond conventional pooling: as children move between age groups, classrooms can be filled through internal flows rather than costly external search, further reducing enrollment delays. Together, verification and mixed use offer a way to expand effective capacity in early childhood classrooms, where regulatory and operational constraints make adding physical capacity particularly costly.
item.dc:creator: Yueyang Zhong, Jun Li, Senthil Veeraraghavan

item.title: Adaptive Node Distribution via Probability Density Functions for Birkhoff Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimisation
item.description: arXiv:2610.12827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pseudospectral methods are a powerful framework for spacecraft trajectory optimisation that rely on fixed, problem-independent collocation nodes such as Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes. These nodes are located according to polynomial root distributions, which can result in insufficient resolution in regions of high dynamical activity, such as those encountered during collision avoidance manoeuvres. This paper presents an adaptive node distribution strategy for Birkhoff pseudospectral trajectory optimisation, where the collocation nodes are placed according to a probability density function derived from the thrust magnitude profile of the spacecraft. By concentrating nodes in regions of high dynamical variation, the proposed method simultaneously achieves feasibility preservation and improved convergence with fewer nodes in a collision avoidance case study when compared to the universal Birkhoff method, with Model Predictive Control serving as an independent validation comparator. The case study highlights the practical consequences of inter-node constraint violations and validates the adaptive node scheme as a robust and efficient alternative for fuel-optimal spacecraft manoeuvre design.
item.dc:creator: Andrian A. Yasintus, Xiaofeng Wu

item.title: When Solvers Get Moody: Quantifying and Predicting Performance Variability in Mixed Integer Programming
item.description: arXiv:2610.12876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers are widely used, yet their performance can vary substantially even under seemingly neutral perturbations. Such variability complicates benchmarking, and the interpretation of computational studies. We introduce the Weighted Variability Score (WVS), a robust multi-component metric that aggregates dispersion in normalized runtime, final optimality gap, LP iterations, and branch-and-bound nodes across repeated runs. On a large subset of MIPLIB 2017 instances, each solved in 100 randomized runs under a four-hour limit, WVS reveals a right-skewed distribution with a substantial upper tail: many instances are essentially stable, but some exhibit large variability that is not explained by basic properties alone. Notably, this experiment proved optimality for the open instance 'neos-5045105-creuse' in two SCIP runs. Using static descriptors and root-level features, a tree-based predictor with a gated tail uplift achieves a mean absolute error of 0.058 and Spearman rank correlation of 0.65 on a sealed test split. Feature-importance analysis highlights root degeneracy, matrix structure, coefficient ranges, and presolve reductions as the main drivers of high WVS. Because variability is systematic and partially predictable from inexpensive early-run features, our findings offer a practical tool for preemptive tuning and lay a foundation for fairer evaluation of new algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Mourchid Adegbindin, Brenda Dietrich, Jamol Pender, Andrea Lodi

item.title: Robust Halo Orbit Stationkeeping Under Missed Thrust Events and Maneuver Execution Errors
item.description: arXiv:2610.12906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spacecraft stationkeeping is subject to various operational uncertainties such as missed thrust events, maneuver execution errors, and dynamics modeling errors. Missed thrust events are the most disruptive of these, and current practices mitigate that risk through Monte Carlo-driven heuristics and conservative margins that offer no formal safety guarantees and do not scale to multiple missed thrust events. This paper models these unplanned thruster outages through the Markov Jump System framework, and represents maneuver execution errors and dynamics linearization errors as bounded multiplicative noise. The resulting closed-loop system is a linear time-varying periodic Markov jump system with multiplicative noise, for which Lyapunov-like mean square stability and periodic set invariance conditions are derived. A linear matrix inequality-based optimal controller synthesis framework then designs a periodic, mode-dependent mean-square stable feedback policy that respects path constraints with probability one. The framework is demonstrated on the Earth-Moon 9:2 near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO), under both impulsive and low-thrust propulsion, and on a Saturn-Enceladus $L_1$ NRHO using impulsive propulsion. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the spacecraft recovers from an arbitrary number of missed thrust events while respecting path constraints, and that the multiplicative noise model introduces additional robustness to maneuver execution error and linearization error.
item.dc:creator: Shaurya Shrivastava, Kenshiro Oguri

item.title: A volume-controlled level-set method for topology optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.12922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topology optimization typically involves a geometric volume/mass constraint due to the limited use of material. As a popular technique for topology optimization, the level-set method typically employs the Lagrange method, the penalty method, or the augmented Lagrangian approach to address the volume constraint. This requires careful parameter tuning and may lead to non-monotonic changes in the objective. In this paper, we present a new volume-controlled level-set method for topology optimization. By imposing a scalar weighted volume?compatibility constraint in a modified Stokes-type extension-regularization problem, the velocity is made volume compatible at the beginning of each frozen transport interval. At the continuous level, we prove that the initial rate of change of the regularized volume vanishes and that the subsequent frozen-velocity drift is of order $T^2$; under a narrow-band assumption, the corresponding constant is independent of the smoothing parameter. For the discontinuous Galerkin spatial semi-discretization of the level-set transport equation, we derive a quantitative regularized-volume drift estimate that displays the dependence on the smoothing parameter, spatial mesh size, transport time, and discrete velocity. The effectiveness of the present algorithm is demonstrated through the minimum compliance problem for linear elasticity, the eigenfrequency maximization for structural vibration, and the minimum energy dissipation problem for Stokes flows.
item.dc:creator: Wei Gong, Zhenmin Zhang, Shengfeng Zhu

item.title: A Palais-Smale type condition for optimal control problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an optimal control problem with a general control constraint and a fixed initial state, for which convexity assumptions are absent. To establish the existence of optimal pairs, we introduce a control version of the Palais-Smale type condition adapted from critical point theory and prove that optimal pairs exist under this condition (see Theorem 2.1). Subsequently, we verify that a specific class of optimal control problems satisfies our Palais-Smale type condition (see Proposition 2.1). Furthermore, as an application, we present an example (Example 3.1) and show that, to the best of our knowledge, no existing result can be applied to establish the existence of an optimal pair in this case (see Section 3.1.1). Example 3.2 shows that finitely many Pontryagin maximum principle candidates do not guarantee the existence of an optimal control. Finally, Example 3.3 demonstrates that the proposed Palais-Smale type condition is sufficient, but not necessary, for the existence of optimal controls.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Michel Coron, Li Deng, Xu Zhang

item.title: Tight Guarantees for Static Policies in Vehicle Sharing Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.13089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study pricing in a vehicle sharing network with $N$ locations and $C$ vehicles, motivated by on-demand bike, scooter, and car sharing, as well as robotaxi and ride sharing services. Customers request directed trips between locations, with travel times following general distributions, and leave without service if no vehicle is available. Pricing affects both demand for trips and the distribution of vehicles across locations. Computing an optimal dynamic pricing policy is challenging because the system state depends on the number of vehicles available at each location and in transit (including how long they have been traveling), motivating the use of simple static policies that offer a fixed price for each trip. For any number of vehicles and locations, we establish a tight performance guarantee for static pricing relative to optimal dynamic pricing. The guarantee holds for any concave objective functions (including revenue rate) and general travel time distributions. Our tight guarantee is bounded below by $ \frac{C}{C + \min \{ C -1, \sqrt{ CN} \} }$ (over 50%), achieving the first universal, non-asymptotic constant factor guarantee. We also prove that the optimal static policy can be efficiently computed by solving a convex optimization problem. Finally, we extend our performance guarantee to the setting with supply redirection.
item.dc:creator: Adam N. Elmachtoub, Jiaqi Shi

item.title: Representing the Non-dominated Set of Multi-objective Optimization Problems with Polyhedral Ordering Cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.13141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the literature, research on representing the non-dominated set has focused almost exclusively on multi-objective optimization problems with Pareto-dominance. However, general ordering cones are used to incorporate preferences of decision makers into the optimization process and to model other specific types of optimization problems, such as ordinal optimization problems. In this work, we consider several representation approaches based on representation relations in the context of multi-objective optimization problems with polyhedral ordering cones. Our main research question is whether existing theory and solution approaches developed for the Pareto case can be used to address the more general setting.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Weuste, Michael Stiglmayr

item.title: Optimal Control of Prox-Regular Sweeping Processes with Variable Time
item.description: arXiv:2610.13327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper is devoted to a broad class of optimal control problems governed by constrained sweeping processes with controlled dynamics, controlled prox-regular moving sets, and variable time included in the optimization process. Employing an advanced version of the method of discrete approximations, we verify its well-posedness with appropriate strong convergence of feasible and optimal solutions. This approach leads us to considering a parametric family of discrete-time controlled sweeping processes, which are reduced in turn to nondynamic mathematical programs with special types of geometric and functional constraints. Invoking powerful tools of first-order and second-order variational analysis and generalized differentiation, we derive necessary optimality conditions for discrete-time and then---by passing to the limit over the diminishing step of discretization---continuous-time controlled sweeping processes. A crucial role in our device is played by explicit coderivative evaluations of set-valued mapping associated with the sweeping dynamics. In this way, we establish novel necessary optimality conditions for local minimizers of continuous-time controlled sweeping processes that contain absolutely continuous and BV adjoint arcs, local and global maximization conditions, $L^2$ active set multipliers, vector measures generated by sweeping and control constraints, and free-time transversality condition expressed through the averaged Hamiltonian. For suitably selected multipliers, we also obtain nondegenerate forms of these conditions when the optimal trajectory starts on the boundary of the moving set. The efficiency of the obtained results is illustrated by some examples related to practical modeling.
item.dc:creator: Tan H. Cao, Boris S. Mordukhovich, Trang Nguyen, Thi Phung

item.title: An Optimal Control Approach to Finite-Time Stabilization of Linear Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a finite-time stabilization method for the integrator chain via optimal control techniques by introducing a tailored cost function. We analyze key properties of the resulting value function to derive the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. Numerical simulations illustrate the effectiveness of the approach.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 23rd IFAC World Congress, International Federation of Automatic Control, Aug 2026, Pusan, South Korea

item.title: Utility-Based Recovery Risk Measures: Redundancy and Approximation for Portfolio Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.13454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recovery risk measures incorporate explicit liability-recovery requirements into asset-liability risk assessment. We study their specialization to optimized certainty equivalents (OCEs), allowing the underlying utility specification to vary across recovery levels and encompassing Recovery Average Value at Risk (RecAV@R) as a special case. For finite recovery specifications, we use the dual penalty representation to characterize redundant recovery regimes and derive position-independent screening conditions. For a subfamily of the Cressie-Read power-divergence family, including entropic and truncated-quadratic specifications, we obtain an exact characterization on atomless probability spaces: universal redundancy is equivalent to a two-dimensional convex-hull condition involving recovery levels and divergence-scale parameters. On such spaces, universal redundancy for RecAV@R reduces to pairwise dominance, whereas for power-divergence OCEs it can arise from the joint effect of several recovery regimes. For nonlinear OCE utilities, we develop a certified piecewise-linear approximation framework for portfolio optimization. In finite-scenario models, the approximating problems are finite-dimensional linear programs, while utility approximation errors transfer directly to the Recovery OCE, yielding explicit error bounds and convergence rates. Uniform approximation over the portfolio domain further implies convergence of optimal values and stability of optimal solutions. A numerical asset-liability study illustrates the effects of recovery-dependent risk preferences and the accuracy and convergence of the approximation.
item.dc:creator: Justin Pl\"uckebaum, Stefan Weber

item.title: A Scalable Learned Iterative Solver for Nonlinear MPC via Temporal Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2610.13480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) can be applied to large nonlinear systems with complex objectives while enforcing constraints, but the cost of solving the underlying optimization problems limits real-time application for systems with fast dynamics or many states. Neural networks can reduce this online cost by approximating the control law, but may violate constraints and typically require many precomputed optimizer solutions for training. The learning-based iterative solver for constrained optimization (LISCO) instead learns to predict primal-dual steps toward satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions through self-supervised training without precomputed solutions, but its dense, monolithic architecture grows with the prediction horizon. We remove this horizon dependence by exploiting the temporal structure of the problem in the solver architecture, which makes the network size independent of the horizon while leaving the training loss and the solver iteration unchanged. A closed-loop resampling strategy further aligns the training distribution with closed-loop operation at no additional sampling cost. On an economic NMPC benchmark of a CSTR cascade, the proposed solver scales to larger problems than monolithic LISCO and achieves median speedups of up to a factor of four over IPOPT. In closed loop, it achieves comparable control performance to IPOPT with no observed constraint violations.
item.dc:creator: Lukas L\"uken, Sergio Lucia

item.title: Stationary Ergodic Mean-field Games of Constrained Singular Controls
item.description: arXiv:2610.13544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a stationary ergodic mean-field game of scalar type where the representative player controls a diffusion through two-sided singular controls exerted only at the jump times of an independent Poisson process. For each mean-field parameter, we solve the novel constrained ergodic singular control problem, proving that the optimal policy is of threshold type: the diffusion is reset at Poisson arrival times to the nearest boundary point of an interval. Our explicit probabilistic derivation of the stationary distributions induced by Poissonian threshold singular controls is a key contribution of independent interest. This distribution is used to construct the mean-field fixed-point map. We prove existence and uniqueness of the stationary mean-field equilibrium by combining the stationary density with the monotonicity and continuity of the optimal thresholds in the mean-field parameter. The model provides a tractable framework for a case study of partially reversible investment with singular adjustments under exogenous intervention constraints.
item.dc:creator: Giorgio Ferrari, Jukka Lempa, Neofytos Rodosthenous, Harto Saarinen

item.title: Lower Bounds for Randomized Linear-Oracle Optimization over Strongly Convex Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.13590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent results [arXiv:2602.04378, arXiv:2602.22608] have established worst-case objective-error lower bounds of order $1/T^2$ after $T$ linear minimization oracle (LMO) calls, matching the upper bound [arXiv:1406.1305] in its dependence on $T$ and thereby resolving a long-standing open question. Upon close inspection, however, both lower bounds are somewhat brittle. The first [arXiv:2602.04378] applies only to the standard Frank--Wolfe algorithm, and, as we show, its prescribed slow exact-line-search trajectories can amplify sufficiently small initialization errors exponentially, corresponding to roughly one additional bit of initialization accuracy per iteration. The second [arXiv:2602.22608] obtains lower bounds for any deterministic LMO-based first-order method via a resisting oracle that adversarially adapts to the queries of the algorithm. In both cases it is conceivable that randomization may circumvent these lower bounds; in particular, neither establishes a lower bound for unrestricted randomized first-order LMO methods. We close this gap by proving an $\Omega(L\operatorname{diam}(S)^2/T^2)$ distributional lower bound for randomized first-order linear minimization oracle methods over strongly convex sets. While our construction reuses the family of [arXiv:2602.22608], our proof characterizes the conditional distribution of the hidden permutation after adaptive queries and bounds the expected decrease of a combinatorial statistic controlling optimizer variance. We further show that the same error threshold holds with probability at least $3/4$ and yields a stopping-time tail bound.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Pokutta

item.title: Relaxed Centralized Circumcentered-Reflection Methods for Convex Feasibility: Convergence and Finite Termination
item.description: arXiv:2610.13713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Projection methods are among the most widely used techniques for solving convex feasibility problems due to their simplicity and robustness. However, classical projection-based algorithms and existing circumcentered-reflection methods generally provide only asymptotic convergence. In this paper, we introduce a relaxed version of the centralized circumcentered-reflection method (cCRM) obtained through an extrapolation of the circumcenter step. We first analyze the two-set case and then extend the proposed approach to the successive framework for multiple convex sets, including under- and over-relaxation and a backtracking strategy. The convergence analysis establishes Fej\'er monotonicity and global convergence under suitable conditions, while local error-bound assumptions yield linear convergence and standard regularity assumptions imply superlinear convergence. Motivated by finitely convergent projection methods based on perturbed feasible sets, we further investigate a perturbed relaxed formulation designed to achieve finite termination. Numerical experiments show good practical performance, comparable to and competitive with the finitely convergent PACA method. The results also provide clear numerical evidence of finite termination in the tested instances.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Guigues, Roger Behling, Adriana Henarejos

item.title: Stabilized SQP Method for Convex Piecewise Linear-Quadratic Composite Optimization Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the local convergence analysis of the stabilized sequential quadratic programming method for a class of composite optimization problems with convex piecewise linear- quadratic (CPLQ) modeling functions. We demonstrate that an appropriate second-order sufficient condition (SOSC) -formulated for composite problems- alone is sufficient to guarantee local superlin- ear convergence of the primal-dual sequence generated by this method. Furthermore, we examine the relaxation of the SOSC and show that it can be replaced with a weaker noncriticality of the associated Lagrange multiplier, provided, the modeling function is polyhedral and a relative interior condition is satisfied. We also present counterexamples showing that the relative interior condition is indispensable and that this relaxation fails for general CPLQ modeling functions.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen T. V. Hang, Ebrahim Sarabi

item.title: Estimation, Sensitivity Analysis, and Optimization of Distortion Risk Measures via Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.13751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a simulation-based method for the estimation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization of distortion risk measures (DRMs), a class of performance measures that capture a wide range of risk attitudes through an underlying distortion function. Existing simulation approaches often approximate DRMs using numerical partitions or empirical distributions. We show that, when the distortion function is piecewise polynomial, the nonlinear structure of a DRM can be handled exactly, without introducing distortion discretization error, using only simulated system outputs. This representation enables the development of a computational method that integrates finite-difference techniques for sensitivity analysis and for solving a broad class of differentiable risk-based optimization problems. Under suitable conditions, we establish strong consistency and convergence rates for DRM estimation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization. We further extend the approach to non-polynomial distortion functions through polynomial approximation. Numerical experiments on synthetic and calibrated financial examples demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach across a range of applications.
item.dc:creator: Hao Cao, Jian-Qiang Hu, Jiaqiao Hu

item.title: Geometry-Aware Multi-Objective Optimization: Norm-Constrained Oracles with Entropic Weight Updates
item.description: arXiv:2610.13773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiple-gradient descent is typically formulated in Euclidean geometry, whereas matrix-aware optimizers use directions induced by other norms. We analyze a single-loop multi-objective method combining a norm-constrained linear minimization oracle with entropic updates of task weights. For any finite-dimensional norm pair, we establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ ergodic stationarity rate in the deterministic setting, deriving the required trajectory gradient bound from smoothness and lower-boundedness in the unregularized case. With stochastic gradients and a bounded-gradient assumption, one persistent blended-gradient momentum buffer yields an $O(T^{-1/4})$ rate whose leading term has no explicit dependence on the number of tasks. We also establish static regret for the inner weighting objective on arbitrary bounded gradient sequences and, with entropy regularization and a weight floor, iteration-wise inner-gap control after burn-in while retaining ergodic stationarity, conditional on a trajectory gradient bound. The optimal blended gradient can be nonunique in spectral and sign geometries, motivating a selection-independent inner gap. Our analysis extends the spectral construction studied by concurrent MOON to general norms. Experiments compare the method with existing multi-task optimizers and examine its oracle, weighting, and momentum choices.
item.dc:creator: El Mahdi Chayti, Alireza Mirrokni, Martin Jaggi

item.title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization with Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.13787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present new algorithms for stochastic optimization problems in which the objective is neither smooth nor convex, subject to a convex constraint set. Our algorithms return a $(\delta,\varepsilon)$-Goldstein stationary point, as recently defined for constrained problems by Liu et al. (2024), with improved complexities, and are the first to achieve optimal convergence rates for this task in several settings. In particular, we design projection-based and projection-free algorithms that achieve a $\widetilde O(\delta^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using stochastic gradients, which we show to be optimal, and a $\widetilde O(d\delta^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using zeroth-order queries, which is also optimal in its dependence on the dimension $d$ and improves over prior work. Notably, our lower bound is given in terms of the Frank-Wolfe gap and holds even for smooth problems, which is of independent interest. These results show that in nonconvex stochastic optimization, the convergence rate is degraded neither by the presence of constraints nor by nonsmoothness. Our analysis is based on a reduction to online linear optimization, extending a related technique from unconstrained optimization.
item.dc:creator: Gon Buzaglo, Guy Kornowski

item.title: Adaptive Variance Reduction without Knowing Oracle Smoothness
item.description: arXiv:2610.13799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variance reduction improves the convergence rate of stochastic non-convex optimization under the average smoothness condition. Existing adaptive variance reduction methods are especially designed for average smoothness and do not adapt to standard smoothness. In this paper, we study how one algorithm can adapt to these two settings and the noiseless setting without knowing the smoothness constants or the variance bound. Given the gradient budget $T$, we develop a two-phase method. The first phase compares two independent gradients and switches to normalized momentum when their difference exceeds a threshold. This phase provides both a candidate with standard smooth and noiseless guarantees and also ensures a bounded expected function gap for the second variance reduction phase. The resulting rates are $O(T^{-1/3})$ under average smoothness, $O(T^{-1/4})$ under standard smoothness, and $O(T^{-1/2})$ without noise. When $T$ is unknown, we propose a method with two paths that attain the corresponding rates with logarithmic factors in the stochastic settings. Here, we use a variance reduction path to deal with average smoothness and employ the AdaGrad-Norm for standard smoothness and noiseless setting. Neither method restarts from the initial point or requires a growing number of oracle calls in each round.
item.dc:creator: Wei Jiang, Yibo Wang, Zechao Li

item.title: Warm-IP: A Path-Following ADMM Warm Start for Interior-Point Quadratic Programming
item.description: arXiv:2610.13805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interior-point (IP) methods are powerful second-order optimization algorithms but can make slow progress during early iterations. We propose Warm-IP, a hybrid framework that combines a path-following variant of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with a primal--dual IP method. The ADMM phase generates a warm start that remains close to the central path, enabling the subsequent IP phase to rapidly refine the solution to high accuracy. We evaluate Warm-IP on a diverse collection of real-world and synthetic quadratic programming (QP) instances and compare it with leading commercial solvers (MOSEK and Gurobi) and open-source solvers (Clarabel, PIQP, and OSQP). We also curate and release a new benchmark of large-scale QPs from cancer radiotherapy treatment planning, built from real patient data and provided in canonical QP form, with instances containing hundreds of thousands of constraints. Warm-IP substantially outperforms existing solvers on large-scale problems. On the large-scale radiotherapy benchmark comprising 60 lung cancer cases, for example, Warm-IP solves an instance in 47 seconds on average with no failures, while the strongest competitors, MOSEK and Gurobi, average 55 seconds with failures on 23\% of the cases and roughly 240 seconds with no failures, respectively. To support reproducibility and future benchmarking, we publicly release the implementation and benchmark data through a \href{https://github.com/Radiotherapy-Optimization/Warm-IP}{GitHub repository}. These results demonstrate that appropriately warm-started IP methods can combine the rapid initial progress of first-order methods with the high-accuracy convergence of second-order methods.
item.dc:creator: Babak Aslani, Mojtaba Tefagh, Gourav Jhanwar, Masoud Zarepisheh

item.title: A Network Simplex Framework For Discrete Unbalanced Optimal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.13847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The network simplex method is a classical algorithm for minimum cost flow problems formulated as linear programs, that has attracted recent interest from the optimal transport community. Indeed, discrete optimal transport is a subclass of minimum cost flow for which network simplex techniques compute exact solutions while leveraging the inherent problem sparsity. However, extending these approaches to other, nonlinear optimal transport formulations has yet to be thoroughly investigated. In this paper, we adapt the network simplex algorithm to unbalanced optimal transport. Our proposed framework is applicable to various unbalanced formulations, and can be implemented explicitly in the most common cases, including semi-unbalanced optimal transport. The resulting algorithms are memory-efficient, and perform competitively with existing approaches, as shown by our experiments on a range of transport and barycenter calculations.
item.dc:creator: Gaetano Agazzotti, Antonin Chambolle, Cl\'ement W. Royer

item.title: On the Five-Point Case of Mordell's Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.12504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For five complex points $z_1,\ldots,z_5$ satisfying $\sum_i|z_i|^2=5$, Mordell's discriminant inequality states that $\prod_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|^2\leq5^5$, with equality precisely for a unit regular pentagon, up to rotation and permutation. We organize its proof around a direct comparison of discriminant values. A global maximizer gives a centered stationary configuration, whose coefficient equations reduce the generic case to two quartic branches. On each branch, the absolute value of a cubic polynomial gives the original discriminant objective after accounting for the normalization scale. Exact rational interval bounds exclude both branches from the maximum, and the exceptional coefficient cases leave the regular pentagon. The argument determines the maximizing configuration without reconstructing all stationary shapes. We have completed a full Lean formalization of the five-point inequality and both directions of its equality condition, including all reductions and finite checks used in this proof.
item.dc:creator: Tiancheng Xu, Guowei Dou, Wensheng Yu

item.title: Fix What's Wrong, Keep What's Right: Hallucination Repair for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.12529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored to automate operations research modeling, reduce modeling time and lower the expertise barrier to optimization based decision support. However, this process often introduces inconsistencies between generated artifacts and the original problem, which we refer to as optimization modeling hallucinations. Despite progress in general-purpose hallucination mitigation, optimization modeling poses a distinct repair challenge: restoring fidelity to the original problem through coordinated model-code updates. We introduce OPT-Kraken, a training-free hallucination repair framework. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first post-hoc framework for repairing hallucinations in LLM-based optimization modeling artifacts. It extracts problem requirements and instance data, localizes errors by checking problem-model fidelity, model-code consistency, and data grounding, and selects repair granularity by the affected scope. For local repair, category rules and instance evidence are compiled into contracts specifying permitted edits, expected effects, and protected content. Experiments on established optimization modeling benchmarks show positive gains across automatic modeling frameworks and fine-tuned models. On zero-shot artifacts from multiple base models, OPT-Kraken effectively repairs optimization modeling hallucinations while preserving initially correct artifacts. These results demonstrate effective and controlled repair for LLM-based optimization modeling artifacts.
item.dc:creator: Jiageng Wu, Chao Shen, Zihan Guo, Junyan Shao, Zongyan Zhang, Jie Song, Zhong Li, Mingyang Sun

item.title: Variational neural transport for aggregation-diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a neural transport framework for nonlinear, nonlocal aggregationdiffusion equations arising in chemotaxis, polymer dynamics, and related applications. Based on the Onsager variational principle, we reformulate the governing equation as a constrained optimal control problem, taking the velocity field as the control and evolving the density via the associated continuity equation. The velocity field is parameterized by a neural network trained on the variational objective evaluated along particle trajectories. By coupling the density and generalized score equations into a single system solved via the Euler method, the score function propagates efficiently for loss evaluation. Furthermore, we establish a rigorous error analysis that decomposes the total error into approximation, optimization, Monte Carlo sampling, and time-discretization components, and prove corresponding error bounds. Numerical experiments across several representative models demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed approach.
item.dc:creator: Qianyi Li, Hailiang Liu

item.title: Distributionally Robust Adaptive Iterative Covariance Steering for Small-Body Proximity Operations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous small-body proximity operations require continuous-thrust guidance under uncertain gravity, solar-radiation pressure (SRP), and stochastic disturbances. We combine iterative covariance steering (iCS) with $L_1$ distributionally robust adaptive control ($L_1$-DRAC) to provide risk-aware collision avoidance despite mismatch between the nominal planning model and the true dynamics. Iterative covariance steering plans a nominal feedback policy satisfying distributionally robust conditional value-at-risk keep-out constraints, while $L_1$-DRAC compensates for dynamics uncertainty and bounds the residual distributional mismatch through a Wasserstein radius used by the planner. In $\mathbf{1000}$ paired Monte Carlo trials with gravity, SRP, and diffusion mismatch, $L_1$-DRAC adaptive control reduces the keep-out violation rate from $\mathbf{32.7\%}$ to $\mathbf{0.2\%}$ and the physical collision rate from $\mathbf{16.4\%}$ to zero, without actuator saturation.
item.dc:creator: Vivek Khatana, Aditya Gahlawat, Naira Hovakimyan, Petros Voulgaris

item.title: Riemannian Hessian analysis of Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.12833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem are Riemannian gradient descent methods on the sphere under a metric induced by a discrete elliptic operator. We analyze their convergence through the condition number of the Riemannian Hessian at the ground state. Bounds of the Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian give a uniform analysis of these methods for different metrics. The uniform analysis applies to the classical metrics, such as the shifted Laplacian and the energy-adaptive metrics. Inspired by this analysis, we also consider three new metrics. One of them is a Thomas--Fermi metric, whose condition number is bounded uniformly in the interaction strength for the one-dimensional harmonic trap and whose iteration count does not grow in the Thomas--Fermi regime in the numerical tests. The performance suggested by our analysis is consistent with three-dimensional numerical tests with up to one billion unknowns, for both Riemannian gradient descent and Riemannian conjugate gradient methods, whose practical performance is also related to the Hessian condition number. The Thomas--Fermi flow needs the fewest iterations, while the metrics inverted exactly by tensor-product solvers are the fastest in computational time on one GPU card.
item.dc:creator: Shixin Zheng, Xiangxiong Zhang

item.title: AI-Mediation in Retail Markets: Revenue Effects and Assortment Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.12917v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI shopping assistants increasingly influence which products consumers consider. We study retail assortment planning under AI mediation, where a retailer chooses a catalog, an AI intermediary forms a customer-facing shortlist, and the customer chooses from that shortlist according to a multinomial logit model. We consider both deterministic mediation, in which the AI follows a fixed segment-specific ranking, and stochastic mediation based on the Plackett-Luce model. Empirically, we construct a dataset of product rankings from leading AI models, estimate Plackett-Luce ranking models, and evaluate their predictive performance on held-out assortments. Combining these estimates with synthetic customer preferences, we find that accounting for AI mediation can materially change optimal assortments and revenue. Across the tested capacity configurations, ignoring mediation yields mean revenue losses between 2.52% and 11.37% relative to the PL optimum. A much simpler deterministic plug-in, based only on the ordering of fitted AI utilities, performs substantially better, with mean losses of at most 0.53%. Motivated by this performance, we study assortment optimization under deterministic mediation. We characterize its computational complexity and show that, for any fixed number of customer segments, the problem admits a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme.
item.dc:creator: Omar El Housni, Marouane Ibn Brahim

item.title: Sequential Conformal Calibration under Recursive Selection
item.description: arXiv:2610.12937v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conformal prediction provides finite-sample, distribution-free coverage guarantees that can support decision-making in specific settings. In multistage problems, earlier decisions determine the populations relevant to later calibration. When later scores are refit using earlier calibration results, reusing those cases for ranking need not preserve exchangeability with a surviving test case. We study sequential conformal calibration with a fresh fold at each stage: conditional on earlier folds, the selected fold scores and the surviving test score are exchangeable. This yields finite-sample coverage guarantees for every prefix of the decision sequence. For atomless survivor score distributions, we derive a universal Binomial-thinned Beta chain for the realized coverage process. Its law depends only on fold sizes and target levels, even under predictable refitting, and yields exact coverage slack, abstention probabilities, and calibration-conditional guarantees. We further characterize the tradeoff between freshness and data reuse. For fixed scores, strict-survivor reuse is exactly valid. For adaptive scores refit using past calibration data, reusing survivors can incur worst-case rank loss, while blocked designs provide an intermediate option between full reuse and stagewise fresh folds. As a case study, we apply the framework to serial multi-echelon inventory problem and propose a sequential conditional-quantile formulation. Each stock level is learned as a context-dependent quantile of cumulative demand among scenarios satisfying earlier no-backlog constraints. We connect these targets to common-shift stationarity and derive decision-level implications for the resulting calibrated policies. In a three-echelon simulation, fresh-fold refitting achieves 81.98% final-prefix coverage against an 81.82% target while reducing mean cost by 5.5% relative to the Bonferroni baseline.
item.dc:creator: Yuning Yang (Georgia Institute of Technology), Zexuan Liu (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign), Tianci Wang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Danlin Li (Georgia Institute of Technology)

item.title: Dynamic Matching with Abandonment: Optimal Guarantees via Static Priority Policies
item.description: arXiv:2610.12991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study stochastic dynamic matching with abandonment, a fundamental model in which agents of different types arrive over time, may abandon the market while waiting, and can be matched in pairs for rewards that depend on their types. No online policy can guarantee more than $0.5$ of the omniscient benchmark, which knows all arrival and departure times. Whether this guarantee is achievable has been a central open problem, even in special cases. We resolve this problem by showing that, on every instance, a simple static priority policy, which is computable in polynomial time, earns at least $0.5$ of the omniscient benchmark. This establishes that the optimal competitive ratio is exactly $0.5$, improving the previous best guarantee of 0.192 for the general model [Li et al. 2026; Collina et al. 2020] Our analysis rests on a key stochastic result, which is a new lower bound on the probability that some agent from a given set of types is available. Building on this bound, we develop two approaches: a primal approach that reads the priorities from an optimal solution of a novel linear program, and a dual approach that assigns a ``value'' to each type, and prioritizes matches with high ``surplus'' (reward minus value of involved agents). These values are the unique solution of a fixed-point equation derived from linear programming duality. We also show that the two approaches are closely connected.
item.dc:creator: Nick Arnosti, Rad Niazadeh, Pranav Nuti, Felipe Simon

item.title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization of the Age of Information with Unknown System Statistics
item.description: arXiv:2610.13142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Inoue, Michel Mandjes, Liron Ravner

item.title: Minimum-Energy Control for Stochastic Linear Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The open-loop minimum-energy control (MEC) problem asks for control inputs that minimize the control energy while ensuring the terminal state reaches a desired value. In this paper, we study the open-loop MEC problem for stochastic linear time-invariant systems. We consider a variety of stochastic constraints that enforce the terminal error to be \emph{small}, and show that Stochastic MEC (SMEC) problem can be formulated as a QCQP. We obtain the optimal solution for SMEC and show that it generalizes the well-known Deterministic MEC problem by introducing novel stochastic variants of controllability and Gramian matrices. Finally, we show that there exists a fundamental lower bound on the optimal control energy which cannot be overcome by increasing the time horizon of the problem.
item.dc:creator: Vaishnavi Sharma, Vaibhav Katewa

item.title: Boundary stabilization of multi-dimensional first-order quasilinear hyperbolic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13577v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the long-time behaviour of multi-dimensional first-order symmetrizable quasilinear hyperbolic systems with nonlinear feedback boundary conditions. Assuming strict interior and boundary Lyapunov inequalities for the linearized system and non-characteristic boundaries, we prove global existence for small initial data and exponential H^s decay, with s>d/2+1 an integer. We consider both bounded smooth domains and flat periodic cylinders, and illustrate the results with physical examples and numerical simulations.
item.dc:creator: Haitian Yang

item.title: An inverse spectral problem for the wave equation with a varying Robin parameter at the boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.13629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An inverse spectral problem for a $(1+1)$-dimensional wave equation with wave speed $c(x)$ is considered. The spectral data consist of the eigenvalues of the Neumann--Dirichlet problem for the operator $-c^2(x)\partial_x^2$ together with their derivatives with respect to a Robin parameter at the boundary. We propose a two-step recovery procedure. In the first step, the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map $\Lambda$ is reconstructed from the spectral data using the results of arXiv/0406582. In the second step, the reconstructed $\Lambda$ is used within the regularization strategy for the boundary control method presented in arXiv:1509.04478. As an improvement, the regularization of the control problems employs a weighted combination of $L^2$ and $H^1$ penalty terms, and we prove a uniform convergence result for the family of optimal controls, thereby allowing the regularization parameters to be tuned simultaneously. We also prove that the forward spectral map, which assigns to a wave speed its spectral data, is Lipschitz continuous, and that the inverse spectral map underlying the reconstruction procedure is H\"older continuous on a subclass of wave speeds. The method is implemented numerically and validated on both smooth and piecewise smooth wave speed profiles. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the recovery of the wave speed exhibits high accuracy and robustness.
item.dc:creator: Antti Hannukainen, Petr Kulikov, Matti Lassas, Lauri Oksanen

item.title: Private and Distributionally Robust Federated Multiclass Classification
item.description: arXiv:2610.13631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fault diagnosis in asset-intensive industries requires multiclass models trained on noisy, sensitive data collected across geographically distributed client sites. Federated learning enables collaborative training without centralizing data, but most approaches do not provide formal privacy guarantees for individual records stored at client sites and can degrade under label noise. To address these limitations, we develop a differentially private, distributionally robust framework for federated multiclass classification that provides sample-level privacy for records stored at each client. We build on a federated Wasserstein distributionally robust multiclass objective with the Crammer-Singer loss, solved using an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based algorithm. To protect the released client updates, our method injects calibrated Gaussian noise into the proximal linearized client updates of both the local model and the local distributionally robust variable before aggregation at the central server, and we quantify the cumulative privacy loss using the moments accountant. We provide per-round sample-level $(\epsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy guarantees and an overall composed privacy guarantee across all training rounds, together with convergence results and an explicit privacy-utility tradeoff. Experiments on simulated industrial fault data and UCI benchmark datasets show that our method outperforms differentially private federated empirical risk minimization and stochastic gradient descent baselines in most tested settings, with the largest gains under strong privacy-induced noise.
item.dc:creator: Andrea P. Hernandez, Michael Ibrahim, Nagi Gebraeel

item.title: Randomized Momentum Transport with Cheap Predictors
item.description: arXiv:2610.13789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Momentum methods such as STORM and second-order momentum track the gradient by adding a transport correction to momentum, at the cost of an extra oracle call per iteration. We introduce randomized momentum transport, which evaluates the correction with probability $q$ and otherwise uses a cheap prediction, with importance weighting that preserves the conditional mean and adds $(q^{-1}-1)$ times the prediction loss to the variance. Under transport-bias, second-moment, and residual-control assumptions, linear minimization oracle (LMO) updates, including normalized, sign, and exact spectral (Muon) directions, retain an $O(T^{-1/3})$ stationarity bound for each fixed $q>0$ with a single-gradient initialization. For unnormalized STORM, some $q<1$ lowers the leading coefficient of our sufficient gradient budget if and only if the gradient-difference noise modulus exceeds the smoothness constant, by at most about $10\%$. An online diagonal predictor admits a regret-to-convergence guarantee. At approximately equal oracle cost, querying a quarter of the corrections lowers the final training loss by $18$ to $43\%$ on MNIST1D and raises the test accuracy of Hessian-vector transport on CIFAR-10 by $1.5$ points.
item.dc:creator: El Mahdi Chayti, Martin Jaggi

item.title: The Riemannian Convex Bundle Method
item.description: arXiv:2402.13670v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the convex bundle method to solve convex, non-smooth optimization problems on Riemannian manifolds of bounded sectional curvature. Each step of our method is based on a model that involves the convex hull of previously collected subgradients, parallelly transported into the current serious iterate. This approach generalizes the dual form of classical bundle subproblems in Euclidean space. We prove that, under mild conditions, the convex bundle method converges to a minimizer. Several numerical examples implemented using Manopt$.$jl illustrate the performance of the proposed method and compare it to the subgradient method, the cyclic proximal point algorithm, as well as the proximal bundle method.
item.dc:creator: Ronny Bergmann, Roland Herzog, Hajg Jasa

item.title: Data-Driven Stochastic Optimal Control in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2407.16407v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper proposes a fully data-driven approach for optimal control of nonlinear control-affine systems represented by a stochastic diffusion. The focus is on the scenario where both the nonlinear dynamics and stage cost functions are unknown, while only a control penalty function and constraints are provided. To this end, we embed state probability densities into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) to leverage recent advances in operator regression, thereby identifying Markov transition operators associated with controlled diffusion processes. This operator learning approach integrates naturally with convex operator-theoretic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman recursions that scale linearly with state dimensionality, effectively solving a wide range of nonlinear optimal control problems. Numerical results demonstrate its ability to address diverse nonlinear control tasks, including the depth regulation of an autonomous underwater vehicle.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence, 1 October 2026, Volume 181, Part 6, Article 115698
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Hoischen, Petar Bevanda, Stefan Sosnowski, Sandra Hirche, Boris Houska

item.title: A Variable Smoothing for Weakly Convex Composite Minimization with Manifold Constraint via Parametrization
item.description: arXiv:2412.04225v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we address a manifold constrained nonsmooth optimization problem involving the composition of a weakly convex function and a smooth mapping under the availability of a parametrization of the manifold. To find a stationary point of the target problem, we propose a variable smoothing-type algorithm by combining the ideas of (i) translating the constrained problem into a Euclidean optimization problem with a parametrization of the constraint set; (ii) exploiting a sequence of smooth approximations of the objective constructed using the Moreau envelope. The proposed algorithm produces a vector sequence by the gradient descent update of a smooth approximation of the objective. In a case where the proximity operator of the weakly convex function is available, the proposed algorithm does not require any iterative solver for subproblems therein. By leveraging tools in the variational analysis, we show the so-called gradient consistency property, which is a key ingredient for smoothing-type algorithms, of the smooth approximations used in this paper. Based on the gradient consistency property, we establish a subsequential convergence guarantee of the proposed algorithm to a stationary point of the parameterized problem and clarify conditions, such as a submersion condition on the parametrization, under which the corresponding point is stationary for the original manifold constrained problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Keita Kume, Isao Yamada

item.title: Leveraging Christoffel-Darboux Kernels to Strengthen Moment-SOS Relaxations
item.description: arXiv:2501.14281v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical Moment-SOS hierarchy allows one to approximate the global minimum of a polynomial optimization problem through semidefinite relaxations of increasing accuracy. For many optimization problems, however, moving to higher relaxation orders quickly becomes computationally prohibitive. While this difficulty is commonly addressed by exploiting structural properties such as symmetry or sparsity, we explore a complementary direction: strengthening a low-order relaxation using information contained in its own pseudo-moment solution. To this end, we leverage Christoffel-Darboux kernels to identify regions that are compatible with the current pseudo-moment information and use them to construct additional polynomial constraints. We propose two mechanisms: the first, denoted $\HH$, is based on successive global Christoffel restrictions, while the second, denoted $\hh$, combines marginal Christoffel information with an available local solution. For $\HH$, we establish a uniform separation property for successive pseudo-moment solutions and geometric convergence of the fixed-order bounds on a particular subclass of knapsack problems. Moreover, for specific Boolean quadratic problems, we derive an explicit $\hh$ selection rule and establish conditions under which the resulting marginal constraints preserve all global minimizers. Numerical experiments on dense and sparse nonconvex quadratically constrained quadratic programs show that the resulting strengthened low-order relaxations can significantly improve the initial bounds, sometimes attaining exactness, while remaining substantially cheaper than solving higher-order relaxations.
item.dc:creator: Sre\'cko {\DH}ura\v{s}inovi\'c, Perla Azzi, Jean-Bernard Lasserre, Victor Magron, Olga Mula, Jun Zhao

item.title: Second-Order Optimization with Asynchronous Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2510.15714v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Second-order methods make fast progress per iteration, but forming and factorizing the Hessian often dominates their wall-clock time. We study \emph{Split-Client}, a task-parallel design in which a curvature client factorizes Hessians in the background while a gradient client takes cubic-regularized steps with the most recently published matrix, so that curvature cost appears as a delay rather than as blocking time. For delayed exact Hessians, we prove a first-order stationarity bound that depends on the average age of the curvature rather than its maximum, using an overlap count and a weighted Hardy inequality that allows any bounded-error initial matrix; the analysis extends to subsampled and uniformly inexact curvature. Under a fixed-cost model, the resulting wall-clock bound matches the scaling of optimally tuned Lazy Hessian without choosing a reuse period. In experiments on two LIBSVM datasets, an implementation decreases the objective earlier in wall-clock time than Lazy and Vanilla cubic Newton, with the largest gains at intermediate accuracy.
item.dc:creator: El Mahdi Chayti, Martin Jaggi

item.title: Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization from Noisy Comparisons: Unbiased Gap Estimation and the Price of Preference Feedback
item.description: arXiv:2602.05622v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the minimization of $L$-Lipschitz, possibly nonsmooth and nonconvex $f:R^d\to R$ from noisy pairwise comparisons: comparing $x$ and $y$ returns a bit equal to $1$ with probability $\sigma((f(y)-f(x))/\tau)$, for a known link $\sigma$ and temperature $\tau$, and the goal is a $(\delta,\epsilon)$-Goldstein stationary point. We give an exactly unbiased estimator of the gap $f(y)-f(x)$ whenever $\sigma^{-1}$ is analytic on a lens in the complex plane, as for the logistic, probit and cauchit links: compare the pair until the outcome changes and return $\pm\tau$ times a partial sum of the expansion coefficients of the inverse link, the harmonic number of the run length for the logistic link. It uses at most $1+1/(1-\alpha)$ comparisons in expectation, $\alpha$ the largest queried success probability, and has second moment of order the gap squared plus $\tau^2$. With randomized smoothing and the online-to-nonconvex conversion this gives $O\big(d\,(1+d\,C_{link}/\kappa^2)\,L^2\Delta_f/(\delta\epsilon^3)\big)$ comparisons when $\Delta_f\ge L\delta$, where $\kappa$ is the ratio of the largest queried gap to $\tau$, which the smoothing radius caps at a constant; relative to the optimal rate $O(dL^2\Delta_f/(\delta\epsilon^3))$ for noisy value oracles, comparisons cost a factor $d/\kappa^2$. We prove that any comparison-based method needs $\Omega(d^2\tau^2/(\epsilon^2\delta^2))$ comparisons on a smooth convex subclass once $d\gtrsim(\epsilon\delta/\tau)^2$: in the comparison-noise-dominated regime the bounds agree in $d$ and $\tau$, and a factor $\Delta_f/(\delta\epsilon)$ remains open. Experiments illustrate the estimator's cost and variance and the $d^2$ growth of the gradient-estimator second moment.
item.dc:creator: El Mahdi Chayti, Taha El Bakkali, Omar Saadi

item.title: RanSOM: Second-Order Momentum with Randomized Scaling for Constrained and Unconstrained Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2602.06824v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Second-order momentum corrects the lag of momentum behind the current gradient with a Hessian-vector product (HVP), but existing corrections need either a Lipschitz Hessian or extra forward and backward passes at an auxiliary point. We show that randomizing the step length removes this trade-off: if the step is exponentially distributed with mean $\eta$, a Stein-type identity makes $\eta$ times one HVP at the new iterate an estimate of the gradient change that is unbiased in expectation over the step, and this HVP shares its forward pass with the next gradient. The resulting method, RanSOM-E, works with normalized, sign, and Muon-type steps, and a Beta-distributed variant, RanSOM-B, keeps Frank-Wolfe iterates feasible. For objectives with Lipschitz gradient and heavy-tailed gradient and Hessian noise with tail indices $p, q \in (1,2]$, RanSOM-E attains the optimal oracle-complexity exponents for every pair $(p,q)$, including $p \neq q$, without a Lipschitz Hessian or clipping ($\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ for $p = q = 2$). On CIFAR-10 with ResNet-20, we detect no accuracy difference from existing second-order momentum methods, and its mean update time is lower than that of the auxiliary-point method.
item.dc:creator: El Mahdi Chayti, Mohamad Fakhouri

item.title: Featurized Occupation Measures for Structured Global Search in Numerical Optimal Control
item.description: arXiv:2603.16231v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Numerical optimal control is split between globally structured but dimensionally intractable Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) methods and scalable but local trajectory optimization. We introduce Featurized Occupation Measures (FOM), a finite-dimensional primal--dual interface where HJB subsolutions guide primal search and primal occupation data can inform certificate refinement. Explicit and implicit realizations, based on finite Liouville tests and rollout-sampled residuals, are proved asymptotically consistent with the exact occupation-measure LP. FOM also identifies when HJB-type certificates avoid full state-space representation. For factor graphs induced by compatible passivity-based interconnections, blockwise HJB inequalities yield block-additive OM-dual certificates, including blockwise approximate variants. The curse of dimensionality is then shifted from state dimension to interconnection topology. Approximate certificates remain reusable under time shifts and bounded model perturbations, with explicit degradation bounds. A static obstacle-avoidance benchmark illustrates how tighter certificates improve sample-based global search.
item.dc:creator: Qi Wei, Jianfeng Tao, Haoyang Tan, Hongyu Nie

item.title: An Inexact Trust-Region Method for Structured Nonsmooth Optimization with Application to Risk-Averse Stochastic Programming
item.description: arXiv:2604.07216v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a trust-region method for efficiently minimizing the sum of a smooth function, a nonsmooth convex function, and the composition of a convex Lipschitz continuous function with a smooth function. Optimization problems with this structure arise in numerous applications including risk-averse stochastic programming and subproblems for nonsmooth penalty nonlinear programming methods. Our algorithm permit the use of inexact value and derivative information, enabling the solution of infinite-dimensional problems governed by, e.g., partial differential equations (PDEs). We prove global convergence of our method and under additional regularity assumptions, demonstrate that the sequence of iterates accumulates at a stationary point of our target problem. We demonstrate our method's efficiency on two PDE-constrained optimization examples, showing that its performance is invariant to the PDE discretization size.
item.dc:creator: Drew P. Kouri

item.title: The Method of Ellipcenters for strongly convex minimization
item.description: arXiv:2605.12820v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work is about ME, the Method of Ellipcenters. ME was recently introduced by these very authors as a first order accelerated scheme for unconstrained minimization. Its iterates are all centers of ellipses carefully designed to somehow capture ill-conditioning of the underlying optimization problem. In the first article on ME, we were able to prove that it converges with linear rate when the objective function is quadratic and strongly convex, while here we derive convergence for any differentiable strongly convex objective. This investigation was inspired by the great performance of ME in quadratic minimization against steepest descent with exact line search, FISTA, Barzilai-Borwein and Conjugate Gradient. The experiments we carry out now, make ME even more attractive from the numerical point of view. On top of that, the theory seems promising for quite more general settings.
item.dc:creator: Roger Behling, Ramyro Correa, Eduarda Ferreira, Vincent Guigues

item.title: Stochastic Compositional Optimization via Hybrid Momentum Frank--Wolfe
item.description: arXiv:2605.15350v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stochastic compositional optimization minimizes $F(f(x), x)$ over a compact convex set when the inner map $f$ is available only through noisy samples. We propose Hybrid Momentum Stochastic Frank--Wolfe, a projection-free method for outer functions $F$ that are jointly convex and Lipschitz but not necessarily differentiable, such as maxima, CVaR, and norms. The method tracks the Jacobian and the value of $f$ with momentum, using a Taylor correction for the value, and passes the tracked linearization to a generalized linear minimization oracle. Under finite-variance noise, it attains an expected generalized Frank--Wolfe gap of order $K^{-1/4}$ for non-convex objectives and, when the linearized models minorize the objective, a last-iterate primal error of order $K^{-1/3}$. The analysis extends to heavy-tailed noise without clipping, with separate moment orders for values and Jacobians. With an exact oracle, the method reduces to the deterministic method of Vladarean et al. (2023).
item.dc:creator: El Mahdi Chayti, Mohamad Fakhouri

item.title: Provable Parameter-Free Fixed-Point Algorithms with Linear Convergence Rates
item.description: arXiv:2608.09022v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop provable parameter-free fixed-point algorithms for contractive mappings, with an emphasis on automatically exploiting hidden contractivity without requiring prior knowledge of the contraction factor. Our first method is a parameter-free variant of the Halpern fixed-point iteration with no line-search, bisection, or prior estimate of the contraction factor, while retaining essentially the same per-iteration computational cost as classical fixed-point schemes. We establish explicit linear convergence rates for both the fixed-point residual and the distance to the unique fixed point. The second algorithm is also a parameter-free Halpern method, but it requires a line-search procedure to find a local estimate for the contraction factor, which may need a few additional operator evaluations. This method also enjoys explicit linear convergence guarantees. We further extend these ideas in two directions. First, using the relation between Halpern iterations and Nesterov-type accelerated fixed-point schemes, we derive parameter-free Nesterov-type (three-term) variants that inherit linear convergence in the contractive setting. Second, by combining the proposed fixed-point schemes with Tikhonov regularization, we obtain new methods for solving cocoercive equations and establish an iteration complexity of $\mathcal{O}({\epsilon^{-1}\log(\epsilon^{-1})})$ for computing an $\epsilon$-solution, provided that a valid lower bound on the cocoercivity constant is available. Numerical experiments on several examples demonstrate that the proposed algorithms are competitive with, and often outperform, existing adaptive fixed-point methods. In particular, the methods successfully exploit contractive behavior when it is present on the selected nonexpansive test problems.
item.dc:creator: Quoc Tran-Dinh, Pham Ngoc Anh, Ha Manh Tien

item.title: Circuit-Embedded Feeder-State Reconstruction for Low-Voltage Distribution Networks under Extreme Measurement Sparsity
